Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, can the source-image paper and cup be identified, and is that paper visibly stuffed inside that cup?
node.criteria: Pass only if the edited image provides enough visual evidence to identify the same paper and cup shown in the source and shows the paper placed inside the cup with evidence it has been stuffed into it. Fail only if both objects are identifiable and the paper is visibly outside the cup or merely on its rim. Unknown if either object's identity, or their placement, cannot be established.
node.binding: Anchor “the paper” and “the cup” to the objects in the source image. Do not treat a visually different-looking item or object in the edited image as the same object without sufficient evidence.

node_traces.evidence: The source shows a white paper-like item and a blue cup, but the edited image shows a blue printed item and a reddish object. There is not enough visual evidence to identify these as the same paper and cup from the source or establish that the paper was stuffed inside the cup.

fulfillment: The node already encodes the key rubric distinction—completion, progress, and unresolved evidence—so do not relax those criteria to force the reference label. The trace is valid uncertainty, not a transport or schema failure: both supports were queried successfully, but their evidence does not establish object identity or progress. Improve the binding/evidence guidance so the checks compare the source and edited images for plausible continuity of the specific paper and cup, while allowing appearance changes when visual context supports identity. In these images, the source has a white sheet and blue cup; the edit shows a hand-held blue printed item near a reddish object. That mismatch makes identity uncertain, but the hand-held item could still be the paper and the reddish object could be the cup, so it is not affirmative evidence that no requested change progressed. Keep uncertainty available unless the visual evidence actually rules out progress; do not treat low confidence or repeated uncertainty as proof of absence. Ensure the completion and partial-progress supports assess their distinct criteria and that the aggregate can return “no” only when both establish no requested progress, as the rubric requires.
s2: The node’s binding already correctly ties progress to the source paper and cup and preserves uncertainty; do not change the criterion merely to force the reference label. The trace is a valid visual uncertainty, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure. Improve the evidence guidance to compare plausible object continuity and the action relation separately: the source shows a white sheet and blue cup, while the edit shows a hand holding a blue printed item over a reddish object. The item could be the paper and the object could be the cup, but their identities and whether the paper is advancing into the cup are not established. Do not treat color mismatch, proximity, high confidence, or repeated uncertainty as proof of no progress. Keep unknown when identity or action remains unresolved; return no only when the relevant objects are identifiable and visual evidence establishes no requested progress. Preserve distinct completion and partial-progress checks and their aggregation criteria.
